text: Most of this mansion keeps what it sees to itself. You are the quarter that says it out loud. Ashlesha's first pada, its opening quarter, falls to Sagittarius in the chart's ninth division, and the far-aiming sign turns the serpent's perception into candor: you notice the undercurrent and then, unlike your secretive kin, you name it, and name what it means. The Nagas, the serpent spirits who preside over this mansion, are teachers in the old stories as often as guardians, keepers of doctrine along with treasure, and their knowledge moves through you with a teacher's outward pressure. Friends receive honest readings whether or not they requested one, which makes you the mansion's best mentor and its most startling dinner guest. People leave your company knowing something about themselves they had managed not to know, and most come back for more, because the seeing arrives without malice. Loosed from a distance, a truth can sail past the person and strike their tenderest belief, and being right about someone is not the same as being useful to them. Timing is the discipline the archer owes the snake. An observation held until it is asked for lands as a gift; the same observation volunteered mid-soup lands as an ambush, and you can read the difference in a face faster than anyone.

You can wait out anyone. Ashlesha's second quarter joins the mansion's insight to the patience of Capricorn, the sign the ninth division deals it, and the mix produces a negotiator who has read the room twice before speaking once. Where your kin feel undercurrents, you budget them: whose support will matter in a year, which grievance will compound, when a silence is actually an offer. Work with long ladders rewards you, management, law, procurement, any trade where knowing people is capital, and you climb without visible hurry, which is the only way you care to be seen doing anything. The habit of reading people as positions does not always stay at work, and the ones closest to you can spend years being studied when they wanted to be told. They matter to you apart from their usefulness, and you know it. Knowing has never once crossed the table on its own.

The coiled serpent on Ashlesha's emblem becomes, in your quarter, a diagram: a system folded back on itself, studying its own loops. You read people the way an engineer reads a circuit: less what a colleague did, more what the setup made likely. A household or an office can repeat the same betrayal in new costumes for years, and you see the wiring behind the repeats. The widening of the lens comes from Aquarius, this quarter's portion of the ninth division; the mansion's penetrating eye lifts off individuals here and lands on patterns. Family systems, office politics, the choreography of institutions open to you like schematics. The fields that study them, research, analysis, the systems-minded schools of therapy, tend to find you without your applying. The observer's seat is drafty, though. Whoever maps the dance seldom gets pulled into it, and your own feelings can end up filed as one more interesting case, annotated and rarely visited. Patterns also predict crowds far better than persons. The friend in front of you is always partly an exception to whatever rule they belong to, and treating them as an instance is the fastest way this quarter loses people. Underneath the models, the mansion's older skill keeps running: the skin-level read of one particular human. Your best calls come on the days you let it overrule the diagram.

Water is the serpent's second element, and Ashlesha's last quarter swims in it. What your kin observe from the bank, you absorb: a friend's dread arrives in your chest before their news does, and ten minutes beside a stranger can send you home carrying their weather. Pisces has this quarter in the ninth division, and the mansion's boundary work runs in reverse here, since the hardest membrane for you to keep is your own. People feel accompanied by you at a depth that changes them, and the mansion's medicine is clearest in your hands because it is offered as company rather than analysis. The porousness has its hazards: you can lose the seam between your feeling and someone else's, believe a story because you can feel how badly its teller needs it believed, or go blurry for a week after a crisis that was never yours. Ashlesha's native suspicion, corrosive elsewhere, is in your case a tool worth keeping oiled, because an occasional cold look at the facts is what lets the softness stay soft. The direction of your attention was settled early, toward the unspoken. Where it all lands is settled nightly: some of what you absorb comes home with you, and some of it stays at the door.

Aries takes Magha's first quarter in the ninth-harmonic chart, and it sets a founder's temper inside an inheritor's mansion: you honor the line by adding to it. The Pitris, the ancestral fathers who preside over Magha, do not read to you as portraits in a hallway. They were predecessors in office, people who acted, and your instinct is to act in ways they would recognize. In any family or institution you drift toward the posts where the standard has slipped and someone must simply decide. Waiting for seniority chafes. Now and then you take a role the room assumed would be granted by age, and it earns you admiration and resentment in equal measure. First of the name is where you keep landing: first to emigrate, first through university, first to say the unsayable thing at the reunion. Deference does not come naturally, and you can treat an elder's caution as an obstacle when it is actually the archive talking. Your temper flares fastest around questions of respect and cools fast too, though the people singed remember the flare longer than you do. The work of this quarter is a founder's work. Whatever you start becomes, for somebody downstream, the tradition. The day you truly feel that, feel that you are someone's ancestor in rehearsal, your hand steadies better than any living authority could manage.

The ring, the deed, the table that crossed an ocean: things hold the line for you. Magha's second quarter grounds ancestry in Taurus, its stretch of the ninth division, so inheritance means to you what it means to a farmer: land, objects, recipes, accounts, the material spine of a family. You are the relative who keeps the house everyone else calls home, repairs the watch instead of replacing it, knows what the plot is worth and will not sell. Stewardship this concrete builds real shelter, and the cousins who tease you about the museum you live in will one day be glad it existed. Objects can also hold you, though. A house can become an argument nobody is allowed to end, and keeping the dead's furniture is easier than doing what the dead would have done with a free Saturday. They were unsentimental owners, most of them. What they wanted from their things was use, and a table is never more honored than when people are eating at it.

Magha's emblem is a royal palanquin, the carried chair, and in your quarter what gets carried is the story. The third quarter draws Gemini from the ninth division, and it makes you the mansion's record-keeper. You can recite the great-grandparents, you interview the elders while there is time, and you know which version of the family legend is polished and which actually happened. Dignity, in your hands, is verbal. You toast, eulogize, and write things down, carrying the line the way the palanquin carries its ruler, on the shoulders of language. That makes you indispensable at the moments families handle worst: the funeral, the estrangement, the question a grandchild finally asks. Curiosity also loosens the mansion's solemnity in you. You honor tradition and still find it funny, which is a large part of why the young ones stay at the table. A story told often enough replaces the memory underneath it, though, and a confidence can turn anecdote before you notice its owner flinch. Wit at a ceremony can read as irreverence to the relatives who needed the ceremony straight. The line trusts you with both of its treasures, the talk and the tact, and it is the tact that decides how long you get to keep the job.

Every clan has one member the dead stay real to, and in your family that is you. Magha's fourth quarter comes home to Cancer in the ninth division, the Moon's own sign, and the ancestors this mansion honors feel to you like company rather than monuments. The grandmother's laugh survives in you along with her name, and a certain smell or song can put a vanished kitchen around you in a second. You keep the emotional estate. Photographs get captioned, the anniversaries of losses quietly observed, the family's tenderness routed through your door. The relatives who roll their eyes at all of it still call you first when someone dies, because you know how to grieve in company. Inheritance in this quarter includes weather. The moods of the line run through you, old fears and unfinished sorrows surfacing a generation late, and it can take years to sort which of your sadnesses are your own and which arrived with the bloodline. The sorting is worth the years, since a grief with a name is lighter than the same grief anonymous. Protectiveness here points backward as well as forward, and you can catch yourself defending the past against fair criticism as if the dead needed a lawyer. They mostly need what you already give, which is remembering. In your rooms the dead keep their place at the table, and nobody who sits down with you has to pretend otherwise.

What you enjoy, everyone knows you enjoy. Purva Phalguni's first quarter is Leo in the sidereal sky and Leo again in its ninth division. The tradition calls the repeat vargottama and reads it as consistency, one register from the inside out, not any added force. So your delight has no backstage. Pleasure completes itself in company for you the way a joke completes itself in laughter. You host, toast, dress, and celebrate at full visibility, and that hands everyone nearby a license to enjoy things without irony. Bhaga presides over this mansion, the god of delight who in one old story loses his eyes at a wrecked sacrifice. The myth's wink fits your quarter: fortune does not inspect credentials before it pours, and at your best, neither do you. Your warmth lands on the intern and the guest of honor alike. With no private room to retreat to, though, indifference reaches all the way in, and an inattentive audience can start to feel like a verdict on your worth. It never was one. An afternoon spent enjoying something with the door shut, unwitnessed and unreported, settles the question better than applause ever has: the wattage was yours the whole time.

Behind every effortless party stands somebody's checklist, and it is yours. Purva Phalguni's second quarter puts craft underneath the mansion's pleasure: the menu tested twice, the playlist sequenced for the arc of the evening, the guest with the allergy remembered without being asked. The workmanship is Virgo's, this quarter's slot in the ninth division, and it gives the lie to the mansion's lazy reputation, because your leisure is produced, and production is labor. You notice the wine served too warm at parties you did not throw, and a perfectionist host can end a beautiful evening privately itemizing its flaws. The guests caught none of them. They felt only the thing that actually matters, that someone had thought about them in advance, and you had that art before you ever alphabetized anything.

The front legs of a couch hold up the end where two people sit down together, and Purva Phalguni's third quarter takes its emblem's geometry personally. Libra, its sign in the chart's ninth part, moves the mansion's delight into the space between people: pleasure, for you, is nearly always relational. The meal tastes better narrated across a table, and the film needs the second seat filled. Your happiest undertakings are duets: a room decorated with someone, a trip planned as a pair, a business run across one desk. You give enjoyment as a form of attention, tracking a companion's mood the way this mansion tracks a party. Being enjoyed by you is one of the pleasanter things that can happen to a person. Your own preference, meanwhile, can go missing inside the duet. Asked what you want, you consult the other face first. Years of gracious deferring can leave you fluent in everyone's appetite but your own, mildly resentful and unsure at whom. Wanting something out loud, first, before taking the room's temperature, is a skill this quarter has to practice deliberately. The couch was built with two seats so that both would be sat in. The companions worth having have been waiting, longer than you think, to hear a want of yours arrive unprompted.

The mansion of the couch ends in its most private corner. Purva Phalguni's last quarter wants deeply rather than widely: one person, one art, one appetite pursued long past the point where your lighter kin would have wandered to the next amusement. The ninth division seats this quarter in Scorpio, and your realest enjoyments run private: guarded, intense, and shared with one other person or with nobody. The sparkling social self this mansion is known for operates in you as a lobby, handsome, welcoming, and nowhere near the vault. Lovers discover the difference and are marked by it; being chosen by you is total. Creative work benefits from the same pressure, since you will go over a piece, a role, a song a hundred times, hunting for the version with blood in it. Jealousy grows quickly where delight and possession share a root, and an ended pleasure gets mourned like a death. Disappointment, which your kin discharge in an evening's sulk, settles in you as brooding that can eat a season. The capacity outlasts all of it, a gift for caring more than is fashionable. Given a person or a craft that can bear its weight, it pays out over decades what quicker pleasures spend in a night.

Your word travels well. Uttara Phalguni's first quarter extends the mansion's reliability past the circle of anyone who could repay it. You keep promises to strangers, and you treat the traveler at the door as if a contract already existed, because to you one does. Sagittarius, the sign the ninth division sets over this quarter, widens the jurisdiction, so duty answers to a principle here rather than to a roster of names. Aryaman, the mansion's presiding god, kept the customs between houses and the courtesies of the road. The old texts gave his name to the Milky Way, the path above every traveler, and your quarter inherits the scale of that image. The great alliances of your life tend to begin as shared conviction rather than shared history. Cause or faith comes first and friendship after, and the bond holds for as long as the conviction does. You are generous on principle, and principle can get loud. You explain your ethics while performing them, you hold people to codes they never adopted, and a favor from you sometimes ships with a small sermon in the box. Range can also outrun capacity, since a person obliged to everyone owes more than any calendar can hold. The stranger on the step wanted shelter, not doctrine, and shelter has always been the part you do best.

Somebody has to run the trust after the wedding toast, and in your circle it is you. Uttara Phalguni's second quarter administers what the mansion promises: the schedule, the budget, the aging parent's affairs, the friendship maintained by standing appointment. Its allotment in the ninth division is Capricorn, and the sign shows in the shape of your caring, help with a start date, a scope, and a successor. Institutions hand you responsibility young, and they are right to. An arrangement can outlive its affection, though, kept running because stopping was never scheduled, and your loyalty deserves an audit by feeling now and then, not only by term. The people who lean on you rarely see the effort; that is the design. It is also why a plain thank-you, when one finally arrives, undoes you a little.

Aquarius governs Uttara Phalguni's third quarter in the ninth division, and it turns the mansion's gift for alliance toward the group: the friend circle, the cooperative, the union, the congregation, whatever set of people has agreed to hold something up together. This mansion's emblem is the back legs of the bed, the pair that does the unseen bearing, and your quarter builds them at scale. You are the member who actually reads the bylaws, the neighbor who organizes the repair fund, the one still answering the group thread in year six after the founders have drifted off. Friendship is your form of covenant; you can love a roomful of people steadily and be genuinely puzzled that anyone calls that cold. Some will call it cold anyway. Breadth spends the attention that depth would have used, and a partner or an old friend can stand inside a crowd you are serving and feel unmet, holding a claim on you that is real but nowhere on the list. The cause can also outlast its point: keeping the association alive can matter to you so much that you keep it alive past anyone's need, out of loyalty to the idea of it. Legs hold up a bed so that particular people can rest there. What stays constant in this quarter is the bearing itself, quiet, plural, and content to be the least famous part of the furniture.

Agreements have a letter and a spirit, and Uttara Phalguni's last quarter reads only the spirit. You sense what a promise was for: the fright underneath a friend's casual request, the marriage inside the mortgage. You honor that purpose even when it means bending the terms everyone else can see. The last of the mansion's ninth-division signs is Pisces, and under it obligation blurs at the borders. You find yourself bound by contracts nobody signed, responsible for sorrows nobody assigned. This is the quarter that forgives a debt and never mentions it again, covers the shift without being asked, stays kind to the relative everyone else has given up on. Grace of that kind steadies more lives than you will ever get an accounting of. It also attracts weight. Word spreads that your yes is easy to reach, the desperate and the merely lazy arrive in equal numbers, and you can be deep into someone's rescue before wondering whether they asked for one. Discernment is not a betrayal of the kindness; it is the banks that keep the river a river. The mansion keeps its word; your quarter keeps the words nobody quite said, and not every one of them was addressed to you.
